comment: Byte budgets for what every conversation pays for when it loads the connector (improvement list M2). tools/list is sent once per conversation; diagram_capabilities and worksheet_capabilities are read before a family's first use. tools/list and per-tool sizes are UTF-8 bytes of the JSON a client receives; capabilities sizes are UTF-8 bytes of the result text a model reads (an error result fails the test). Measured 14 Nov 2026 on main 946e205: tools/list 72,220 bytes (create_worksheet 29,530, create_booklet 20,125); longest description create_booklet, 3,867 characters; capabilities text graph 58,016, bar-model 44,336, triangle 34,494, construction 27,591, cuboids 17,118, number-line 16,154, probability-tree 12,405, every other family under 12,000; worksheet_capabilities 4,812. Graph grew from 39,413 on 657aee1 with shaded inequality regions (#275), gradient triangles (#264) and house-style lines (#307); most of that is the operations schema repeating object shapes, a candidate for trimming. Each budget has about 5% headroom. Lower a budget when a change makes the catalogue smaller; raising one needs a reason in this comment and in the pull request. The family list (diagram_capabilities with no kind) gained topics and notDrawn for M89: 4,698 bytes on 14 Nov 2026. M1/M14 (15 Nov 2026, main 0ce7af7): each family's specSchema and operationsSchema now writes a shape it reuses once, in its own $defs (only when that is smaller); capabilities text graph 58,016 to 25,653, bar-model 25,894 (44,336 before v3 only) to 20,616, cuboids 17,118 to 10,879, triangle 34,494 to 32,663, construction 27,591 to 26,780, number-line 16,154 to 15,675. Budgets lowered to about 5% headroom; cuboids now uses the default. Charts raised from the default to 17,900 on 15 Nov 2026: pie charts, pictograms and scatter graphs became chart kinds (S-2, S-3, S-5), scatter with its own points, axes and line-of-best-fit schema; measured 17,055 bytes after M1/M14. Raised to 19,000 on 15 Nov 2026 for the scatter table of values and broken axes (Tim asked for both for exam coverage): measured 18,141 bytes. M10 (15 Nov 2026): every top-level spec field has a one-line description; bar-model capabilities 21,995, so its budget rises 21,600 to 23,100 (about 5% headroom). Raised list to 5,300 on 15 Nov 2026 for the angles family (its summary and topics, about 400 bytes) and to 5,900 for the area family (about 400 bytes; measured 5,706); every family adds a line here. Raised on 15 Nov 2026 for beside (two items in one card row, Tim's A7.04 marking): every leaf item gains an optional beside flag, in card and part items of both tools; measured tools/list 78,250, create_worksheet 31,941, create_booklet 21,383, so tools/list 82,200, create_worksheet 33,500 and create_booklet 22,500 (about 5% headroom). The flag carries no description of its own; the tool descriptions explain it once. Raised list 15 Nov 2026 for two more families, factor trees (N-5) and sample space diagrams (P-3): each adds a summary and topics, 6,451 bytes. Graph raised 26,900 to 32,400 on 16 Nov 2026 for transformations and vectors (worked solutions for every paper need them, Tim 16 Nov 11:57): an image object with its translate/reflect/rotate/enlarge transformation and a vector arrow on segments, in both the spec and the operations schemas; descriptions trimmed first; measured 30,861 bytes. Raised to 35,400 the same day for real-life and travel graphs (120 parts): curve objects through points (straight pieces or smooth), reading lines to the axes and an axis letter such as t; measured 33,724 bytes after trimming. Raised to 39,000 the same day for curve working (148 parts): circle objects (x² + y² = r²), tangent segments touching a curve and trapezium strips under it; measured 37,159 bytes. Raised to 43,200 the same day for equation curves in the Graph tool (quadratic, cubic, k/x, exponential and trig graphs in degrees), so tangents, strips, lines and readings apply to them for graphical solving, gradients, areas and graph transformations; measured 41,132 bytes. Charts raised to 24,600 on 16 Nov 2026: histograms, frequency polygons and cumulative frequency graphs became chart kinds sharing one grouped table (classes, a true-size graph-paper axis per kind, tables and cumulative frequency readings), needed for 192 exam parts' worked solutions; measured 23,465 bytes, with the axis patch shape written once. Raised list 6,800 to 7,400 on 16 Nov 2026 for function machines (A1.02-A1.05) and, next, written methods (NP2): measured 6,809 with function machines; each family adds about 350 bytes. Nets of 3D shapes (GM2.07, 16 Nov 2026) landed alongside written methods and box plots; nets' summary and topics were trimmed to about 250 bytes first. Raised to 27,400 on 16 Nov 2026: box plots became a chart kind (up to three plots with five hideable values each on a true-size scale, needed for the box plot exam parts' worked solutions); measured 26,050 bytes, the row and scale shapes already shared through $defs. Raised to 29,600 on 16 Nov 2026: stem-and-leaf diagrams became a chart kind (rows of a stem and its leaves with separate hide flags, a key that can be printed, left empty for pupils or left out, and the leaves column width), needed for 19 exam parts' worked solutions; measured 28,231 bytes. Raised list 7,400 to 7,800 on 16 Nov 2026 when box plots and stem-and-leaf diagrams (#404) met function machines and written methods on main: the chart topics and the two new families together measured 7,444 bytes. Charts raised to 31,900 on 16 Nov 2026: time series graphs became a chart kind (up to 24 equally spaced times, each with a label, an optional group such as a year and a hideable value, joined with straight lines on true-size graph paper), needed for the Year 10 SP8 worksheets before Christmas (Tim 16 Nov 15:41); measured 30,379 bytes, the axis shape already shared through $defs. Raised list by 500 on 16 Nov 2026 for the algebra tiles family (A1, A2, A4.02 collecting like terms): its summary and topics; measured 7,928 bytes before nets. create_worksheet raised 33,500 to 35,000 the same day: the algebra-tiles kind joins the diagram kinds a worksheet can place; measured 33,562 bytes. Raised list 8,300 to 9,000 the same day for the geometry figures family (summary and topics, about 400 bytes) on top of algebra tiles and nets. Geometry figures capabilities 17,000 (measured 16,133): seven point placements, each a small schema, plus segments, angles, fills and captions; it is the one family for circle theorems and similar and congruent shapes. Raised on 16 Nov 2026 for spinners, dice and bags (the probability-objects family, needed for the SP3 and SP7 worksheets before Christmas): list 9,000 to 9,500 (its summary and topics, about 450 bytes); tools/list 82,200 to 86,400 (measured 82,255) and get_diagram_svg from the 5,000 default to 5,300 (measured 5,012), as every tool that names the diagram kinds gains one; the server instructions were trimmed to stay under 2,000 characters. Raised list 9,500 to 10,000 the same day for the 3D solids family (summary and topics, about 450 bytes); 3D solids capabilities 20,900 (measured 19,843): six solid shapes, each a small schema, written in both the spec and set_solid, plus points, lengths, angles and two kinds of view; it is the one family for prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, spheres and hemispheres (88 question parts). The server instructions' family list was rewritten more compactly so every family fits under 2,000 characters. Charts raised to 34,600 on 16 Nov 2026 for the SP8 worksheets' exam questions: frequency polygon mistakes (plotting at a class bound, closing the polygon) and a second polygon with a key, two time series with a key, misleading time series (zig-zag choice, curved joins, joining across a missing time) and hidden time labels; measured 32,971 bytes. Ratio tables raised from the default to 13,900 on 17 Nov 2026 for faded tables in booklet lessons (BOOKLET-STANDARD rule N8, Tim 17 Nov 09:43): a hidden heading flag in every heading shape (spec, add_column and set_headings), the answerOnly spec field and the set_answer_only operation; descriptions trimmed first; measured 13,239 bytes. create_booklet raised 22,500 to 23,800 on 20 Nov 2026 for the booklet limits Tim asked to remove (Y11 mock revision, SP7.06, SP8.06): lessonName and lessonBadge on the booklet, given on an answer line (a worked example's own writing on the pupil copy) and answer on a working space (model working, answers copy only), the last two in card and part items; the descriptions gained nothing. Number line raised 16,500 to 18,800 on 21 Nov 2026 for probability scales (a colleague and Tim, 21 Nov 08:02): plain ends with no arrow, words under the line (a word shape in the spec and a set_words operation), fraction and word arrow labels, 10 arrows and 100 tick intervals; descriptions trimmed first; measured 17,892 bytes.
